title: aiwatcher event envelope
description: What a producer publishes. This is the contract between Python/TypeScript agents and the Rust backend; an SDK is a convenience, this file is the agreement. The backend fills in everything a producer leaves out — see RecordedMetadata in the OpenAPI document for the recorded form.

schema_version.description: Contract version. An envelope from a newer contract is rejected rather than half-read.

kind.description: Only events are ingested today. The discriminator is on the wire from day one so adding control commands later is not a breaking change.

event_id.description: Deduplication key; a UUIDv7 or ULID. OMITTING THIS DISABLES DEDUPLICATION for the event: the backend generates one, so a redelivery looks like a new event and double-counts its tokens.

event_type.description: See docs/event-catalog.md. An unrecognised type is stored and streamed live rather than rejected; it simply takes part in no span. So does every eval.* type, deliberately: an evaluation report is a record, not a trace.

occurred_at.description: When the producer observed it, RFC 3339. Distinct from the backend's ingested_at; the gap between them is producer lag.

run_id.description: One execution of an agent. This is what a trace is scoped to, and what the log partitions by. For an eval.* event it is the evaluation id: an evaluation is an execution too, so it gets its own stream and its own partition, and it never appears in the runs list.

conversation_id.description: Groups several runs a user would think of as one conversation. NOT the partition key: one conversation can fan out into parallel runs, and partitioning by it would serialise them.

workflow_id.description: Which orchestration this run is an execution of. A conversation groups runs by who is talking; a workflow groups them by what is being executed, so the same graph is comparable across sessions. Read from data.workflow as a fallback, for producers that predate this field.

sequence.description: Producer-side counter within the run. Gaps here are the only way to notice a producer that dropped a batch.

trace_id.description: W3C Trace Context trace id. Derived from run_id when omitted, deterministically, so a replay reproduces it.

span_id.description: Derived from (trace_id, span key) when omitted. A start and its end must resolve to the same span id — which they do automatically when both carry the same data.call_id and agent_id.

parent_span_id.description: Explicit parenting. When omitted the backend parents onto the innermost open container span (agent, else run) of the same run.

correlation_id.description: Groups an entire flow; inherited unchanged by everything the flow causes.

causation_id.description: The direct cause. Roots itself on correlation_id when nothing seeded it, so 'what caused this' always has an answer.

data.description: Type-specific payload. Free-form so an SDK can add a field without a backend release. Fields the backend reads are listed below; anything else is stored and shown but not interpreted.

call_id.description: Distinguishes concurrent LLM or tool calls inside one agent. Without it, two parallel calls collapse into one span.

tool_call_id.description: Accepted as an alias for call_id.

duration_ms.description: Used to back-date the span start when only an end event was ever sent.
